punchline: A half-inch layer of clay at Gubbio held far more iridium than the rock around it.
thirty_sec: Walter Alvarez found a thin clay layer at Gubbio that told him nothing until his father suggested measuring iridium. The 1980 Science paper found 30 to 160 times background levels at three sites and argued for a 10-kilometre asteroid; the Chicxulub crater was published in 1991.
question: Which puzzle have you declared a dead end, and what have you never measured about it?
